content.text: **Finding: compliant.** The warranty package meets or exceeds the preferred position on its material terms.

input.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
input.rationale: Section 12 gives us an express conformance-to-Specifications warranty for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and rolling thereafter while Maintenance Services continue — at or above the preferred 12-month software warranty. Real remedies are in place: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no charge under §10(c) Software Repair Service; §7/§8 give us rejection with a full refund of amounts paid if deficiencies are not corrected during acceptance; and §15 preserves recovery of direct damages rather than capping us to a single exclusive repair remedy. Critically for us, the agreement contains no "AS IS" language and no disclaimer of implied warranties, so nothing swallows the express warranty. Noted but not flagged as deviations (minor sub-elements short of preferred wording): there is no separate "professional and workmanlike" warranty for installation, conversion, training and maintenance services, no no-malicious-code warranty and no compliance-with-laws warranty. We would add these if the document is reopened for other reasons, but they do not take the clause below the fallback.
